chunks: And Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a man who had no wealth, so he performed hajj on behalf of another man, or another sent him for hajj; then he later acquired wealth—does hajj remain obligatory upon him? He عليه السلام said: “It suffices for both of them.”

key_terms.أَحَجَّهُ: Another person enabled or sent him to perform hajj.
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: The obligation of hajj in question.
key_terms.مَالٌ: Wealth or financial means relevant to the obligation of hajj.
key_terms.يُجْزِي: It is sufficient and fulfills the obligation.

ai.seo_question: If someone performed hajj while poor on behalf of another person and later became wealthy, must he perform hajj again for himself?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about a financially incapable person who performed hajj on behalf of another or was enabled by another to perform it, and then later became wealthy. The Imam عليه السلام states that the performed hajj is sufficient, indicating that he does not need to perform another hajj for himself.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2870 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from Abu Abdullah (as)

regarding a man who did not have wealth and performed Hajj on behalf of another person or was sent for Hajj by someone else. Then, later, he acquired wealth. Is Hajj still obligatory upon him?
Imam (as) said: "It suffices for both."
